title: How To Build Rapport On The First Day Of School https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2015/08/08/how-to-build-rapport-on-the-first-day-of-school/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin lays out five simple, low-effort strategies for building rapport with a new class starting the very moment students walk through the door on day one. These include personally greeting every student by name at the classroom door, smiling generously despite the traditional advice to withhold warmth early on, sharing a personal or humorous story so students see the teacher as a real person, being open to shared laughter without needing to be a comedian, and promising students that the teacher's own personality and demeanor will remain consistent, including a commitment to never yell or speak disrespectfully. He frames these small gestures as 'game-changers' that, combined with a well-prepared room and detailed rule instruction, create instant likability, trust, and leadership presence. The payoff, he writes, is students who leave excited to tell their parents about their new teacher and a teacher who closes the door on day one feeling quietly triumphant.
points: Personally greeting each student by name at the door makes an immediate positive impact on rapport.
Smiling generously on the first day, contrary to old advice to withhold warmth, builds instant likability.
Sharing a personal or funny story helps students see the teacher as a real person rather than an authority figure only.
Promising consistent personal demeanor, including never yelling, builds trust that pays off throughout the year.
These small first-day gestures, combined with clear rules and a prepared room, create outsized leadership presence and influence.
quotes: Stand at your classroom door and personally say hello to every student as they walk in. Look them in the eye, ask them their name, and then introduce yourself.
The oft-recommended advice that you should never smile the first month of the school year is hogwash. In fact, smiling generously on the very first day is a great way to build rapport.
It’s important on the first day of school for your students to see you as a real person, and not a robot built by the government to tell them what to do.
Promise that you will never yell or speak to them disrespectfully. It’s a simple statement, but so, so powerful—for both them and you.
They create leverage and influence, instant likability and leadership presence. They make your immovable boundary lines of behavior matter to students.
Your students will exit your classroom excited to tell their parents how much they love their new teacher and can’t wait to get to school the next day.
